title: Module 1 Quiz: Introduction to Blockchain Technology

questions.text: What is a key characteristic of a blockchain as a distributed ledger?
options: Only one central server stores the ledger.
Each node holds an identical updated copy and the majority rejects any altered copy.
Nodes can maintain different versions without consensus.
The ledger is stored exclusively on mining devices.
questions.explanation: A blockchain is a distributed ledger shared across many computers, with every node holding an identical updated copy and the majority rejecting any altered copy.

questions.text: What occurs if someone tries to alter an old block in the blockchain?
options: The change is accepted automatically by the network.
The hash of that block changes, breaking the chain and requiring re-mining of all subsequent blocks, which the majority will reject.
Only that block is invalidated while later blocks remain valid.
The network ignores the change and continues processing.
questions.explanation: Each block contains the previous block's signature; altering an old block changes its hash and breaks every link after it, and majority consensus rejects the altered chain.

questions.text: True or false: Blockchain enables cross-border payments to settle in minutes rather than days.
questions.explanation: True. Blockchain-based payments settle in minutes rather than days, compared with traditional transfers that take days.

questions.text: When a buyer scans a supply-chain token or QR code on a product, what can they verify?
options: The product's price in local currency.
The estate origin, harvest date, and history of the product.
The number of employees at the factory.
questions.explanation: Scanning a token or QR code lets a buyer verify the estate origin, harvest date, and history of the product.
